name: Crucible for Plex
subtitle: Native client for your server
promotionalText: New: Trakt scrobbling and scores, and requests through your own Seerr, Overseerr or Jellyseerr, built in and off until you connect them. On iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.
description:
Crucible is a native client for your Plex Media Server on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, built to feel like part of the system: the system player, native menus and Liquid Glass.

SKIP WHAT DOESN'T MATTER
Essentials hides the anime-only episodes of long shows, the ones that adapt no manga chapter: Dragon Ball Super goes from 131 episodes to 110 and Up Next follows. The guides come from Crucible Guides, an open dataset (CC BY-SA). Skip Recap and Skip Preview read your files' own chapters, and Spoiler Shield hides what you haven't seen yet.

YOUR WHOLE PLEX SETUP
Connect Trakt to scrobble what you watch and see its score beside IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes on every title. Connect Seerr, Overseerr or Jellyseerr to request what your server doesn't have, watch it arrive, then play it. Both stay off until you connect them.

PICK UP WHERE YOU LEFT OFF
Home opens on a Resume hero, then Continue Watching, Up Next and Recently Added. Libraries filter by Unwatched, In Progress and genre, with an A–Z scrubber. Search groups results by type with a Top Result.

A PLAYER THAT RESPECTS YOUR TIME
Skip Intro and Skip Credits from Plex markers, audio and subtitle menus, lock screen controls and Up Next that rolls the next episode as the credits start. On iPhone and iPad: Picture-in-Picture and background audio. Direct play when your device can handle the file, automatic transcoding when it can't.

MADE FOR IPAD
A sidebar with every Plex library, layouts for every window from Slide Over to a full 13-inch screen, and several windows at once. With a Magic Keyboard, a menu bar and shortcuts: Command-1 to 4 for the tabs, Command-F to search, Space to play, S to skip the intro.

MADE FOR THE COUCH
The Apple TV app is built for the Siri Remote: a cinematic Home that follows focus, one tab per library, search, and Top Shelf with Continue Watching and Up Next.

TAKE IT OFFLINE
On iPhone and iPad, download movies, seasons or single episodes in the quality you pick. Transfers continue in the background and, on iPhone, show a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.

KNOW YOUR VIEWING
Watch History grouped by day, Statistics with streaks, heatmaps and binges from your Plex history, or with Trakt from everything you watch, and a Year in Review poster you can share.

FREE TO USE, CRUCIBLE PRO TO GO FURTHER
Browsing, search, playback, Trakt and requests are free on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, and so is the Statistics view for the last week. Crucible Pro unlocks unlimited offline downloads, the full Statistics screen with every range and Everything from Trakt, the Year in Review poster, Top Shelf, and approving your household's requests. Pay once or yearly; one purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, with Family Sharing.

TRY IT WITHOUT A SERVER
Choose Try the demo on the welcome screen to explore a fictional library with everything unlocked.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No sign-up, no ads, no analytics. Crucible talks to plex.tv and the server you choose, fetches episode guides as one file shared by everyone, records Crucible Pro purchases with an anonymous Midgar ID, and reaches Trakt or Seerr only once you connect them.

OPEN SOURCE
Crucible is free software under GPL-3.0: https://github.com/guitaripod/Crucible

Crucible needs a Plex Media Server. Plex requires a Plex Pass or Remote Watch Pass to stream from your server away from home. Crucible is an independent app and is not made by, endorsed by or affiliated with Plex, Inc. Plex is a trademark of Plex, Inc. Crucible uses Trakt but is not endorsed or certified by Trakt.

Crucible Pro Annual: billed yearly at the price shown in the app. The subscription renews automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the period. Manage it in your Apple Account settings.
Terms of Use (EULA): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/
Privacy Policy: https://midgarcorp.cc/crucible/privacy
reviewNotes:
WHAT'S NEW IN 2.9.0 (iPhone, iPad and Apple TV; all of it works in the demo)
- Trakt (trakt.tv), optional and off until connected: Settings > Integrations > Trakt > Connect. In the demo a built-in stand-in for Trakt approves the code by itself, so no Trakt account is needed (a real account enters the code at trakt.tv/activate; Apple TV also shows a QR code). Then plays are scrobbled; Mark Watched, ratings and Check In (in a title's menu) go to Trakt; a title's meta line shows Trakt's score beside IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes; Statistics gains a Plex / Everything switch (Everything is Crucible Pro). Disconnect revokes the token. Crucible uses Trakt but is not endorsed or certified by Trakt.
- Seerr, Overseerr or Jellyseerr (a request server the user runs beside their own Plex server), optional: Settings > Integrations > Seerr finds the demo's stand-in; choose Connect. Then You > Watchlist > Night Train to Nowhere (not on the server) opens Request; Search "orchard" lists Glass Orchard under Not on Your Server; The Salt Road's menu offers Request More Seasons; You > Requests lists requests, and the owner can approve Sam's (Crucible Pro). Requests go only to the user's own Seerr; Crucible plays only from the user's own Plex server.
- Also: library sorts by rating source, resume returning to the exact position, a sleep timer that always ends playback.

Crucible is a client for the user's own Plex Media Server and has no content of its own. Plex requires a paid Plex Pass or Remote Watch Pass to stream a server's video away from home (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/), so we cannot give App Review a working account and server. The demo runs a fictional Plex server inside the app instead (Guideline 2.1(a)): no account, server or network needed.

START THE DEMO
On the Welcome screen choose "Try the demo", then "Start exploring". The account types and settings below are under the You tab.

ACCOUNT TYPES IN THE DEMO
1. Server owner (the demo starts as "Demo"): every feature unlocked, plus the owner's tools: Manage in a title's long-press menu and on a library's header (Fix Match, Edit Details, poster and background, scans), Stop Stream in Server Activity, Server Dashboard under You.
2. Plex Home member with a PIN: You > Switch Profile > Sam, PIN 1234. Sam has a watch history of their own and no owner tools.
3. Managed (restricted) profile: You > Switch Profile > Kids, no PIN. Only family titles appear. Switch Profile > Demo returns to the owner.
4. Free install and Crucible Pro: the demo starts unlocked. Turn on You > Preview Free Version to see a free install: Statistics ranges past Week, the Statistics library filter, the Year in Review poster and Top Shelf are locked, and the locks open the paywall. A purchase there (sandbox) unlocks them for real; Restore Purchases is on the paywall.

CRUCIBLE PRO (in-app purchases, StoreKit with Midgar's own engine, MidgarKit)
com.guitaripod.crucible.pro.lifetime, non-consumable, $17.99 until December 7, 2026, then $39.99; com.guitaripod.crucible.pro.yearly, auto-renewable, $7.99 a year, $14.99 for new subscribers from December 7, 2026, no free trial. Both approved; universal purchase covers Apple TV. Playback is never gated. Paywall: You > Crucible Pro, the end of the demo tour, or any lock in the free preview.

OTHER NOTES
Local network access is requested to reach servers on the user's home network; App Transport Security allows arbitrary loads because Plex servers on private addresses use HTTP or self-signed HTTPS. No third-party SDK. Crucible keeps an anonymous Midgar ID (iCloud Keychain) for Crucible Pro purchases, and only once the user connects them talks to their own Trakt account and their own Seerr, as the privacy policy and App Privacy answers describe.

whatsNew.IOS:
Trakt and Seerr, built in and off until you connect them in Settings › Integrations.

Trakt: connect with a code and Crucible scrobbles what you play (downloads too, once you're back online) and sends what you mark watched, your ratings and check-ins. Every title shows Trakt's score beside IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, Letterboxd and MyAnimeList on its meta line, under each source's mark. If Trakt's own Plex sync already records your plays, Crucible asks which one should, so nothing counts twice. With Crucible Pro, Statistics adds Everything: what Trakt knows you watched in other apps, on streaming services or at the cinema, counted once, and the shared poster says so.

Seerr, Overseerr and Jellyseerr: Crucible finds the Seerr next to your Plex server and signs in with your Plex account. Request a watchlist title your server doesn't have, or a show's missing seasons; Search adds a Not on Your Server shelf to request from, and watchlist cards say whether a title is on the server, requested or on its way. Each request joins your Plex watchlist, so Watchlist Arrivals tells you when it lands. Requests under You lists yours, and with Crucible Pro whoever approves requests can approve, decline and retry everyone's. No Seerr yet? Set Up Seerr walks you through it, and Crucible reaches it at home and over Tailscale.

Also new:
- Library sorts name the source of each rating (Rotten Tomatoes, IMDb, TMDB) and add an audience rating sort.
- Detail pages appear whole instead of filling in as you look.
- Resume returns exactly where you stopped: a transcoded stream no longer reported twice its position, which ended episodes early and moved Continue Watching ahead.
- The sleep timer ends playback when it says it will, even during an Up Next countdown, the credits or a pause.
- Settings never cut a value short.

Crucible uses Trakt but is not endorsed or certified by Trakt.
